request.system:
You help test a checker of explanations of credit-risk models. You get the facts about one fitted model and an explanation of it that is correct. Change exactly one sentence so that it states something about the model that the facts do not support: a subtle, plausible error that a careless writer could make. For example: a strength one class too high or too low, the wrong direction, a rank off by one, a jump or a peak in the wrong place, an interaction the facts do not show, or "the data do not settle" about something the facts settle.

- Keep the rest of the sentence, its style and its length. Do not mark or explain the change in the text.
- Change only one statement in that sentence.

Return one JSON object: `sentence_id` (the sentence you changed), `sentence` (its new text), and `claim`: the one DSL claim that states your error, with the feature names exactly as in the facts, in a form from this reference:

| Words in the text | DSL claim | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| "a strong / moderate / weak effect" | `strength("x") == "strong"` (or "moderate", "weak") | share of the model's importance at least 15% / 5% to 15% / 2% to 5%, and an effect the data can detect |
| "a weak to moderate effect", "a moderate to strong effect" | `strength("x") in ("weak", "moderate")` | the share lies somewhere in the classes named |
| "at most a weak effect", "a small effect" | `strength("x") in ("negligible", "weak")` | share below 5% |
| "hardly matters", "negligible" | `negligible("x")` | share below 2%, or no detectable effect and a small share |
| "the most important", "the second most important" | `rank("x") == 1` | rank among the features by importance |
| "second or third", "among the three most important" | `rank("x") in (2, 3)`, `rank("x") in (1, 2, 3)` | one of consecutive ranks |
| "about 30% of the importance" | `share("x") == approx(0.30)` | share of importance, within 2 points or 10% |
| "matters more than" | `effect("x") > effect("y")` | x's importance exceeds y's |
| "risk increases with x" / "decreases" | `direction("x") == "increasing"` (or "decreasing") | rises from the 5th to the 95th percentile, with no reversal the data can detect |
| "risk mostly increases with x" | `direction("x") == "mostly_increasing"` (or "mostly_decreasing") | rises overall, with a detected reversal on at most 10% of the data |
| "risk generally increases with x" | `direction("x") in ("increasing", "mostly_increasing")` | either of the two above |
| "risk jumps at x = 0.43" | `threshold("x", at=0.43)` | one sharp step near that value, at least half of the curve's range |
| "risk peaks at x = 36" | `peak("x", at=36)` | the highest point of the curve lies near that value, with lower values on both sides |
| "the effect of x grows with y" | `interaction("x", "y", pattern="amplification")` | the effect of x is larger when y is high |
| "the effect of x reverses with y" | `interaction("x", "y", pattern="sign_flip")` | the effect of x has opposite signs at low and high y |
| "x and y do not interact" | `interaction("x", "y", pattern="none")` | no interaction of practical size |
| "the data do not settle whether ..." | `unsettled(<any claim above>)` | the facts leave that claim open at this sample size |

Rules of the DSL: one claim per line, exactly in the forms above; numbers as plain numbers; a set of values is a tuple of neighbouring values; `unsettled(...)` wraps one other claim. A pair of features can be named as "x & y" in `strength`, `share`, `negligible` and `effect`.
messages:
The facts about the model:

Model: a gradient-boosted tree model of depth 2 (XGB2), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (5,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `utilization`: revolving credit utilization: the share of the credit limit in use (0 to 1).
  Share of importance 38.3% (95% band 28.1% to 59.2%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 0.279: -0.7; 0.279 <= x < 0.628: +0.052; 0.628 <= x < 0.745: +1.37; x >= 0.745: +2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +3.13, 95% band [+2.14, +3.51]).
- `n_delinquencies`: number of past delinquencies on the credit file (0 to 6).
  Share of importance 22.5% (95% band 14.4% to 29.6%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.4; >= 1: +0.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +1.03, 95% band [+0.47, +1.11]).
- `dti`: debt-to-income ratio (0 to 0.6).
  Share of importance 8.1% (95% band 0.6% to 11.3%); rank 3 to 6 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.32 (95% band [+0.01, +0.61]) from x = 0.0312 (5th percentile) to x = 0.571 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `income`: annual income in US dollars.
  Share of importance 6.6% (95% band 1.4% to 9.5%); rank 3 to 7 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): falls by 0.38 (95% band [-0.61, -0.04]) from x = 21,800 (5th percentile) to x = 111,000 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `history_months`: length of the credit history in months.
  Share of importance 5.4% (95% band 0.4% to 9.1%); rank 3 to 7 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): falls by 0.30 (95% band [-0.57, -0.00]) from x = 23.8 (5th percentile) to x = 343 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `feature_a`: an application attribute (standardised).
  Share of importance 1.5% (95% band 0.0% to 4.3%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.10, 95% band [-0.29, +0.15]).
- `age`: age of the applicant in years.
  Share of importance 1.1% (95% band 0.0% to 5.2%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.04, 95% band [-0.09, +0.42]).
- `n_inquiries`: number of recent credit inquiries.
  Share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 2.5%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.09, 95% band [-0.01, +0.22]).
- `feature_b`: an application attribute (standardised).
  Share of importance 0.5% (95% band 0.0% to 4.3%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.01, 95% band [-0.32, +0.13]).

Interactions: the model has 22 pairs. The larger ones:
- `utilization & n_delinquencies`: share of importance 3.2% (95% band 1.4% to 5.4%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.103 to 0.746: +3.03 (95% band +2.15 to +3.51) when `n_delinquencies` = 0, +3.41 (95% band +2.01 to +3.64) when `n_delinquencies` = 3.
  Effect of `n_delinquencies` from 0 to 3: +0.92 (95% band +0.40 to +1.18) when `utilization` = 0.103, +1.30 (95% band +0.29 to +1.38) when `utilization` = 0.746.
- `utilization & age`: share of importance 1.5% (95% band 0.0% to 2.0%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.103 to 0.746: +3.08 (95% band +2.09 to +3.74) when `age` = 23.7, +3.16 (95% band +2.01 to +3.50) when `age` = 72.2.
  Effect of `age` from 23.7 to 72.2: -0.14 (95% band -0.22 to +0.36) when `utilization` = 0.103, -0.06 (95% band -0.57 to +0.37) when `utilization` = 0.746.
- `utilization & income`: share of importance 1.4% (95% band 0.2% to 2.6%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.103 to 0.746: +3.03 (95% band +2.02 to +3.44) when `income` = 21,800, +3.20 (95% band +2.10 to +3.59) when `income` = 111,000.
  Effect of `income` from 21,800 to 111,000: -0.38 (95% band -0.69 to -0.04) when `utilization` = 0.103, -0.21 (95% band -0.61 to +0.02) when `utilization` = 0.746.
- `n_delinquencies & dti`: share of importance 1.2% (95% band 0.0% to 2.4%).
  Effect of `n_delinquencies` from 0 to 3: +1.06 (95% band +0.47 to +1.22) when `dti` = 0.0312, +0.97 (95% band +0.46 to +1.14) when `dti` = 0.571.
  Effect of `dti` from 0.0312 to 0.571: +0.37 (95% band +0.01 to +0.69) when `n_delinquencies` = 0, +0.28 (95% band +0.00 to +0.70) when `n_delinquencies` = 3.
- `utilization & history_months`: share of importance 1.1% (95% band 0.3% to 3.9%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.103 to 0.746: +3.35 (95% band +2.10 to +3.59) when `history_months` = 23.8, +3.09 (95% band +2.05 to +3.55) when `history_months` = 343.
  Effect of `history_months` from 23.8 to 343: -0.30 (95% band -0.73 to +0.00) when `utilization` = 0.103, -0.56 (95% band -0.75 to +0.12) when `utilization` = 0.746.
- `utilization & dti`: share of importance 1.1% (95% band 0.2% to 3.4%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.103 to 0.746: +3.14 (95% band +2.16 to +3.63) when `dti` = 0.0312, +3.01 (95% band +1.92 to +3.43) when `dti` = 0.571.
  Effect of `dti` from 0.0312 to 0.571: +0.39 (95% band +0.00 to +0.76) when `utilization` = 0.103, +0.26 (95% band -0.10 to +0.60) when `utilization` = 0.746.
- `income & feature_a`: share of importance 0.5% (95% band 0.0% to 1.5%).
  Effect of `income` from 21,800 to 111,000: -0.25 (95% band -0.65 to -0.03) when `feature_a` = -1.64, -0.46 (95% band -0.77 to -0.03) when `feature_a` = 1.64.
  Effect of `feature_a` from -1.64 to 1.64: +0.10 (95% band -0.29 to +0.33) when `income` = 21,800, -0.10 (95% band -0.26 to +0.20) when `income` = 111,000.
- `income & age`: share of importance 0.5% (95% band 0.0% to 1.7%).
  Effect of `income` from 21,800 to 111,000: -0.39 (95% band -0.69 to -0.03) when `age` = 23.7, -0.30 (95% band -0.64 to -0.03) when `age` = 72.2.
  Effect of `age` from 23.7 to 72.2: -0.08 (95% band -0.19 to +0.38) when `income` = 21,800, +0.01 (95% band -0.09 to +0.45) when `income` = 111,000.
- `utilization & feature_b`: share of importance 0.5% (95% band 0.0% to 2.0%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.103 to 0.746: +3.10 (95% band +2.14 to +3.50) when `feature_b` = -1.65, +3.14 (95% band +2.14 to +3.53) when `feature_b` = 1.59.
  Effect of `feature_b` from -1.65 to 1.59: -0.01 (95% band -0.45 to +0.11) when `utilization` = 0.103, +0.03 (95% band -0.35 to +0.38) when `utilization` = 0.746.
- 13 further pairs with a share below 0.5% each, together 4.0%.

The explanation, sentence by sentence:

2. The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, with a moderate to strong effect, and default risk increases with it, though it matters less than utilization.
3. The debt-to-income ratio has at most a moderate effect and is ranked third to sixth, with default risk increasing with it; it matters less than the number of past delinquencies.
4. Income and length of credit history each have at most a moderate effect, ranked third to seventh; default risk decreases as income and credit history length rise.
5. The data do not settle whether utilization and past delinquencies interact, while utilization does not interact with income, credit history, debt-to-income, or age, and income does not interact with age.
7. The data do not settle whether utilization and past delinquencies interact, so that question remains open at this sample size.

Change one sentence.
